# pocketid_api_client_access (Resource)

Manages what one OIDC client may do with one API (`pocketid_api`) in Pocket-ID, with the permissions it may request. There are two kinds of access:

- **User-delegated access**: the client calls the API on behalf of a signed-in user. Pocket-ID may ask the user to consent to the permissions.
- **Client access (M2M)**: the client calls the API as itself, with the `client_credentials` grant, and no user. A public client cannot have it, because it cannot keep a secret.

A client with client access gets a token for the API when it asks for one with `grant_type=client_credentials`, `resource=<the API's resource>` and `scope=<permission keys>`. The token's `aud` is the API's resource and its `scope` the permissions that were requested and are granted here; without a `scope`, all the permissions granted. A client without access to the API is refused: with `access_denied` when it asks for the API, and with `invalid_scope` when it also asks for a permission.

The resource sets the client's grants on the API as a whole: a permission that is not listed is revoked, and destroying the resource revokes everything the client has on the API. Its grants on other APIs are untouched. The access to metadata-document clients that the API itself gives is set on `pocketid_api` and is not shown here.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pocketid_api" "orders" {
  name     = "Orders API"
  resource = "https://api.orders.example.com"

  permissions = {
    "read:orders"  = { name = "Read orders" }
    "write:orders" = { name = "Write orders" }
  }
}

# A confidential client that calls the API as itself, machine to machine. It
# asks Pocket-ID for a token with the client_credentials grant:
#
#   grant_type=client_credentials
#   resource=https://api.orders.example.com
#   scope=read:orders
resource "pocketid_client" "backup" {
  name          = "Backup job"
  callback_urls = ["https://backup.example.com/callback"]
}

resource "pocketid_api_client_access" "backup" {
  api_id    = pocketid_api.orders.id
  client_id = pocketid_client.backup.id

  # Client access (M2M). `client_access` is true when permissions are listed.
  client_permission_ids = [pocketid_api.orders.permissions["read:orders"].id]
}

# A client that calls the API on behalf of a signed-in user, and may also act
# as itself with another permission.
resource "pocketid_client" "web" {
  name          = "Orders web app"
  callback_urls = ["https://orders.example.com/callback"]
}

resource "pocketid_api_client_access" "web" {
  api_id    = pocketid_api.orders.id
  client_id = pocketid_client.web.id

  user_delegated_permission_ids = [
    pocketid_api.orders.permissions["read:orders"].id,
    pocketid_api.orders.permissions["write:orders"].id,
  ]
  client_permission_ids = [pocketid_api.orders.permissions["read:orders"].id]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `api_id` (String) The ID of the API (`pocketid_api.id`). Changing it replaces the resource.
- `client_id` (String) The ID of the OIDC client (`pocketid_client.id`). Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `client_access` (Boolean) Whether the client may use the API as itself (machine to machine). Defaults to whether `client_permission_ids` has any permission: Pocket-ID counts a permission as access. Set it to true without permissions for access that gives a token no scope. Pocket-ID refuses it for a public client.
- `client_permission_ids` (Set of String) The IDs of the permissions of the API (`pocketid_api.permissions[key].id`) the client may request as itself. Defaults to none.
- `user_delegated_access` (Boolean) Whether the client may use the API on behalf of a user. Defaults to whether `user_delegated_permission_ids` has any permission: Pocket-ID counts a permission as access. Set it to true without permissions for access that gives a token no scope.
- `user_delegated_permission_ids` (Set of String) The IDs of the permissions of the API (`pocketid_api.permissions[key].id`) the client may request on behalf of a user. Defaults to none.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the grant: the API ID and the client ID, separated by a `/`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A client's access to an API is imported with the ID of the API and the ID of
# the client, separated by a `/`. The ID of a client registered through a Client
# ID Metadata Document is a URL: <api_id>/https://client.example.com/metadata.json
terraform import pocketid_api_client_access.backup <api_id>/<client_id>
```
